stories.title: The Plan: Architecture Firm Corgan Redesigned Its Own Empire State Building Office
stories.excerpt: For 18 years, part of the New York City team at national architecture firm Corgan has called the 54th floor of the Empire State Building home. But, after nearly two decades, even an office in a building as iconic as that one needs a good sprucing up. Corgan’s footprint in the Empire State Building went from 18,714 square feet to 26,035 square feet as part of the year of renovations — during which time the firm’s aviation, data center and corporate interiors teams temporarily relocated. Now the firm’s almost 150 employees — just in that office, mind you — are all back home in a landmark property that has defined the New York City skyline, and they are enjoying a full-floor space that Corgan itself designed. “For a majority of last year, we moved out of the building so that we gutted the entire floor,” said Brent Capron, studio design director at Corgan. “We now can accommodate up to 162 in this office. A big part of the expansion was the ability to rightsize the amenity program, and also modernize that for what we’re going to need for the future.” The office takes inspiration from the famous building, which opened in 1931 as the world’s tallest skyscraper. Interiors incorporate Art Deco themes from the 1920s and 1930s while also including elements that are original to the space, such as refinished original elevator doors, exposed and painted riveted steel columns, and original 1931 terrazzo flooring that was rediscovered during construction. “We wanted to tie ourselves to this place and be part of that Empire, and city spirit,” Capron said. “The team came up with a concept called Echoes of Deco, and really taking a modern take on some of the patterns and themes that you see in Art Deco architecture. You see it in the repeating vertical patterns, the color schemes, and mixed metals. stories.summary: Architecture firm Corgan completed a major redesign and expansion of its 54th-floor office in the Empire State Building, growing its footprint by ~40% while temporarily relocating staff during a full gut renovation. The project incorporated Art Deco design language alongside modern sustainability systems and now houses approximately 150 employees. The expansion signals continued demand for premium, iconic office space in Manhattan despite broader office sector headwinds.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. This is a single-tenant office renovation in an existing iconic tower—not a signal of new supply, demand drivers, or capital availability affecting apartment markets. The project does not indicate broader Manhattan office-to-residential conversion potential or market momentum.

stories.title: NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission Moves Headquarters to 250 Broadway
stories.excerpt: AmTrustRE has signed the New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC) to 39,000 square feet at 250 Broadway for its new headquarters. Occupancy is expected in Q1 2027. “We’re proud to welcome the Taxi and Limousine Commission to 250 Broadway as they establish their new headquarters,” said Jonathan Bennett, president of AmTrustRE. “Our relationship with the City of New York spans multiple leases across our portfolio, and this lease builds on that longstanding partnership. As we continue to invest in and elevate 250 Broadway, TLC’s decision to make this building their home reflects the building’s premier location, modern infrastructure and enduring appeal to institutional tenants.” AmTrustRE was represented by Anne Holker in-house, along with Brad Gerla, Michael Rizzo, and Alex Benisatto of CBRE as landlord broker. The tenant was represented by Gus Field of Cushman & Wakefield. The post NYC Taxi and Limousine Commission Moves Headquarters to 250 Broadway appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NYC TLC leases 39,000 sq ft at 250 Broadway, occupancy Q1 2027
AmTrustRE landlord; institutional tenant demand supports office asset valuations

stories.summary: The New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission has signed a 39,000-square-foot lease at 250 Broadway with occupancy expected in Q1 2027, representing a significant institutional tenant win for the office market. AmTrustRE, the building's owner, leveraged its portfolio relationship with the City of New York to secure the deal. The transaction underscores continued demand from government and institutional tenants for modern Manhattan office space.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. However, stable government tenancy in Downtown Manhattan office assets can stabilize real estate valuations and capital markets confidence in lower Manhattan, which indirectly supports mixed-use development feasibility. Not a demand driver for apartments.

stories.title: Co-Living Complex Near UCLA Will Become Student Housing
stories.excerpt: Colliers completed the $8,500,000 sale of a multifamily complex located at 1775 Beloit Ave. in West Los Angeles. Vice chair Kitty Wallace represented both the buyer, UCLA Housing Group, and the seller, Enterprise Bank. The sale was completed through a court-appointed receivership process. UCLA Housing Group plans to convert the property into student housing. Constructed in 2023, the seven-story, Type II co-living property comprises approximately 18,000 square feet and 16 residential units totaling 48 beds. The transaction closed at $531,250 per unit, or approximately $472 per square foot. “The transaction reflects a broader shift underway across the Los Angeles multifamily market,” said Wallace. “Over the past decade, developers increasingly delivered co-living communities to provide attainable housing near the region’s largest employment and education centers. Following the pandemic, however, Los Angeles experienced a prolonged period of muted rent growth while household incomes, replacement costs, and home prices continued to climb. As new development has become increasingly difficult and the forward construction pipeline continues to contract, investors are placing greater emphasis on acquiring well-located existing assets below replacement cost in anticipation of improving supply-demand fundamentals.” Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. bullets: UCLA Housing converts 2023-built co-living property (16 units, 48 beds) to student housing
$8.5M sale; $531K per unit or $472/sq ft reflects distressed receivership pricing
Los Angeles multifamily pipeline contraction and muted rent growth pressure co-living economics
stories.summary: UCLA Housing Group purchased a newly built co-living complex near campus in West Los Angeles for $8.5 million through a receivership sale, planning conversion to student housing. The property—built in 2023 with 16 units and 48 beds across 18,000 sq ft—sold at $531,250 per unit, a distressed valuation. The transaction exemplifies a broader shift: as LA rents stagnated post-pandemic while construction costs rose, co-living's attainable-housing model became economically unfeasible, forcing investor pivot to alternative uses.
stories.impact: West Los Angeles/UCLA submarket: This signals contraction in new supply pipeline and investor withdrawal from build-to-hold multifamily development due to cost-to-rent mismatch. Co-living distress removes product diversity from the market, tightening supply flexibility. For developers, it confirms LA's forward pipeline will shrink and rents must accelerate materially to justify new construction at current labor and material costs; existing student-housing demand near major universities remains stable, but institutional buyers are capturing it at lower valuations.

stories.title: Development Site with Uncommonly Long Frontage Sells in Brooklyn
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets closed the $23.5-million sale of 1150 Broadway, a residential development site in the Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood of Brooklyn. The team of Brendan Maddigan, Steve Rutman, Mike Mazzara and Ethan Stanton represented the seller, A-PLUS International Realty, and negotiated directly with the buyers, Brooklyn-based YS Developers and Rabsky Group. Situated at the crossroads of Bedford-Stuyvesant and Bushwick, the 26,730-square-foot corner site is zoned for a mixed-use building with apartments, local retail and community facilities. Under the City of Yes for Housing Opportunity program, it offers up to 133,917 square feet of as-of-right zoning floor area. The property also sits within a federally designated Qualified Opportunity Zone and is eligible for the 485-x tax abatement program. The site features approximately 475 feet of wraparound frontage along Lafayette Avenue, Kosciuszko Street, Kossuth Place and Broadway. “Sites with this much frontage, this level of zoning flexibility and direct subway access rarely come to market in Brooklyn, and our marketing process generated significant interest from developers looking to establish a presence in the neighborhood,” said Maddigan. “YS Developers and Rabsky Group have a clear path to deliver a large-scale residential project with an attractive long-term position.” If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. bullets: YS Developers and Rabsky Group acquire 26,730 sq ft Bedford-Stuyvesant corner site for $23.5M

475 feet wraparound frontage, direct subway access, rare availability in Brooklyn neighborhood
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets closed the $23.5 million sale of a 26,730-square-foot development site at the Bedford-Stuyvesant/Bushwick border to Brooklyn-based developers YS Developers and Rabsky Group. Under City of Yes for Housing Opportunity zoning, the corner site is entitled to 133,917 square feet of as-of-right floor area for mixed-use (apartments, retail, community facilities). The property qualifies for 485-x tax abatement and sits in a Qualified Opportunity Zone, with exceptional 475-foot wraparound frontage and direct subway access.
stories.impact: Brooklyn/Bedford-Stuyvesant: This is a textbook entitlement signal. City of Yes zoning liberalization dramatically increased density ceiling and removed approval risk—sellers recognize this and pricing reflects it; buyers now control a shovel-ready mixed-use site. For developers, this confirms Brooklyn's regulatory environment is unlocking value and reducing project friction. Expect increased bid-ask compression as other large-frontage development sites in similarly zoned areas reprice upward and move quickly.

stories.title: Triple-Net AutoZone Sells to Private Investor from LA
stories.excerpt: Hanley Investment Group Real Estate Advisors and Progressive Real Estate Partners arranged the $2.64-million sale of a renovated, single‑tenant AutoZone in Bakersfield. The building, originally constructed in 2013, underwent a full renovation in 2025 and is leased to AutoZone on a new 15‑year triple-net lease. EVP and partner Jeff Lefko and EVP Bill Asher of Hanley represented the seller, Torrey Financial Group, based in San Diego. The buyer, a private investor from Los Angeles, was represented by Greg Bedell, SVP and Managing Director, and Lance Mordachini, Vice President with Progressive Real Estate Partners in Rancho Cucamonga. “We procured an all‑cash, 1031-exchange buyer from Nevada,” said Lefko. “We negotiated a 40‑day escrow and closed at over 96% of the listing price, which reflects the continued depth of demand for essential retail in fast‑growing suburban markets.” Bedell added, “Our buyer was highly motivated and moved quickly because of the long‑term lease, the recent renovation, replaceable rent, and the investment grade strength of AutoZone. This asset checked every box for investors seeking stable, service‑based retail in supply‑constrained California markets.” The AutoZone is located at 1125 Olive Dr. in Bakersfield, occupying an 8,302‑square‑foot building. The post Triple-Net AutoZone Sells to Private Investor from LA appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: AutoZone single-tenant net-lease property Bakersfield sells for $2.64M with 15-yr lease
Property renovated 2025; buyer all-cash 1031 exchange from Los Angeles/Nevada
Strong investor demand for essential retail in supply-constrained California suburban markets
stories.summary: A newly renovated single-tenant AutoZone in Bakersfield, constructed in 2013 and fully upgraded in 2025, sold for $2.64 million on a new 15-year triple-net lease. The all-cash buyer, a private investor from Los Angeles executing a 1031 exchange, was highly motivated by lease duration, recent capital expenditure, investment-grade tenant credit, and supply scarcity. The deal closed at 96% of asking in 40 days, signaling robust demand from individuals seeking stable service retail in fast-growing suburban California markets.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. This is single-tenant net-lease retail in a secondary market—not a supply, demand, capital, or cost signal for apartment development. The strength in suburban retail investment does indicate economic confidence in Bakersfield's growth trajectory, but does not directly affect multifamily underwriting or acquisition strategy.

stories.title: Northern NJ Industrial with Heavy Power Trades to Commerce Park Investors
stories.excerpt: Resource Realty of Northern New Jersey arranged the sale of a high-utility, standalone industrial facility located at 36 Pine St.in Rockaway, NJ. The transaction was brokered and finalized by firm Principals Greg Sabato and Scott Peck, who represented the buyer, Commerce Park Investors. The property encompasses 53,252 square feet of functional industrial space. Suitable for intensive manufacturing, assembly or specialized logistics, the building features heavy-duty infrastructure, including two tailboard exterior dock doors and one drive-in bay. Crucial for modern industrial users, the property boasts heavy power, equipped with a 2,500 amp, 440-volt electrical system capable of supporting heavy production loads. “This single-story property represents a unique opportunity for an operator requiring significant power infrastructure wrapped in a highly functional industrial footprint,” said Sabato. “Heavy power of this caliber – 2,500 amps – coupled with dedicated loading capabilities is an increasingly rare commodity in the northern New Jersey market. Securing this building underscores the sustained demand for spaces that can immediately accommodate a full-range of manufacturing and technical requirements.”  The post Northern NJ Industrial with Heavy Power Trades to Commerce Park Investors appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Commerce Park Investors acquire 53,252 sq ft industrial facility Rockaway, NJ for heavy manufacturing
2,500 amp 440-volt electrical system; two tailboard docks, one drive-in bay—rare heavy-power infrastructure
Northern NJ industrial market supply constraint for heavy-use manufacturing spaces
stories.summary: Resource Realty brokered the sale of a 53,252-square-foot standalone industrial building at 36 Pine Street in Rockaway, New Jersey, to Commerce Park Investors. The single-story facility features exceptional infrastructure: a 2,500 amp, 440-volt electrical system capable of supporting heavy production loads, two tailboard exterior dock doors, and one drive-in bay. Brokers noted that heavy-power industrial space of this caliber is increasingly rare in the Northern New Jersey market and represents a unique opportunity for intensive manufacturing and assembly operators.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Industrial demand and scarcity do not affect apartment markets. However, sustained industrial user competition for power-intensive space in Northern NJ may signal underlying industrial real estate demand and economic activity in the region, which could eventually correlate with population retention and rental demand—but this is indirect and not a primary signal for multifamily developers.

stories.title: Arrow Real Estate Advisors Hires Jeff Weinberg as Managing Director
stories.excerpt: Arrow Real Estate Advisors is adding another experienced veteran to its staff of capital markets experts. The New York-based real estate advisory firm has hired Jeffrey Weinberg as a managing director, Commercial Observer can first report. Weinberg comes from Meridian Capital Group, a firm he co-founded in 1991. Weinberg served as executive vice president, specializing in multifamily and office debt placement. “Jeff has built an exceptional career in commercial real estate and has an unparalleled depth of knowledge and relationships across the industry,” said Morris Betesh, founder of Arrow Real Estate Advisors. “His experience, judgment and entrepreneurial approach align perfectly with Arrow’s platform and culture.” Weinberg’s move is not uncommon. Betesh, previously a senior managing director at Meridian Capital Group, had exited the firm along with 12 team members to form his own capital markets advisory firm. Weinberg told CO that he joined Arrow Real Estate mainly due to the strength of his relationship with Betesh, whom he worked with at Meridian Capital Group for several years. “Morris and I were friends over there, we worked together at the old place, he left a couple of years ago, and I thought this would be a nice fit for me in this stage of life and my career,” said Weinberg. Weinberg was one of the original founding partners at Meridian Capital Group, where his expertise during a three-decade tenure ran from managing client and lender relationships to executing CRE transactions across developments and strategic relationships. He estimated that he has completed more than $1 billion in originations in his career. He told CO that he was attracted to Arrow Real Estate’s ongoing growth and expansion since the company was founded in October 2024. “I knew Morris had a very good team of professionals who know the market very well and I thought it would be a good fit to make my next move,” he said. Weinberg's move follows Betesh's earlier exit from Meridian with 12 team members to form Arrow, and underscores ongoing consolidation and talent reshuffling across commercial real estate debt advisory platforms.
stories.impact: Indirect relevance to multifamily capital. This hiring reflects continued senior-level talent movement in debt placement advisory, which signals liquidity in capital markets hiring and confidence in debt placement demand. However, the shift is primarily a consolidation play between advisory platforms and does not indicate broader changes in debt availability, pricing, or multifamily financing conditions. Monitor for further Meridian departures as a signal of founder/leader confidence in their debt platform.

stories.title: Alexandria Shows Positive Signs After Several Depressed Quarters: Earnings
stories.excerpt: Ailing Alexandria Real Estate Equities is showing signs of improvement as leasing increased over the second quarter of 2026, a hopeful sign of progress after several quarters of declining fundamentals. The life sciences-focused real estate investment trust (REIT) posted earnings Tuesday that show declining balance sheet performance with $73.7 million in net income for the second quarter of 2026 versus $109.6 million during the same period last year. Funds from operations (FFO) was $296.1 million, more than $100 million lighter than in the second quarter of 2025 and down a similar amount from the $396.4 million reported in the first quarter of 2026. Revenue declined from $762 million in the second quarter of last year to $662.7 million for the same period in 2026. Joel Marcus, Alexandria’s executive chairman and founder, however, was more optimistic than in previous quarters, stating that science sectors are improving economically, even if that progress has not yet been reflected on the real estate side. “We’re winning an outsized number of shares of transactions, which is good,” Marcus said during the call. “We have a very well-diversified and strong tenant base. … Very strong leasing in the second quarter from our life science products, service and device sector really depicts shovels and tools of the industry and is almost 40 percent of the leasing volume.” Alexandria leased 1 million square feet of space in the second quarter of 2026, compared to about 647,300 square feet in the first quarter, with about 329,000 square feet being deals that backfilled newly vacant space. In previous quarters, Alexandria executives have pursued dispositions to support the company financially while the life science market recovers. The company sold $170.3 million in assets, including 3825 and 3875 Fabian Way in Palo Alto, Calif., for $163 million in mid-July. However, executive chairman Joel Marcus signaled optimism that science sectors are improving economically even as real estate fundamentals lag. The company posted modest leasing gains, suggesting a turning point, but overall portfolio values and cash generation remain under stress.
stories.impact: Limited direct impact on multifamily development, but notable as a capital markets signal. Alexandria's extended weakness in life sciences real estate (a capital-intensive, speculative segment) reflects broader uncertainty in speculative development financing. Declining FFO and revenue may tighten REIT reinvestment capacity and capital availability across the sector; however, multifamily-focused REITs have generally outperformed life sciences peers, so this does not directly constrain apartment financing.

Viralam found his niche at Emory University, where degrees in finance and real estate placed him at an intriguing crossroads between the business world and entrepreneurship. He landed a job at CBRE after graduation, where he proceeded to spend nearly two decades honing his craft as a real estate strategist and problem solver. Viralam was serving as executive vice president in charge of CBRE’s consulting group in Manhattan when Newmark came a-knocking. Commercial Observer sat down with Viralam in July, just a few weeks into his tenure at Newmark, to discuss his vision for the group, New York’s office occupancy challenges and where real estate consulting slots into the dealmaking mix. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: Can you describe the nature of the real estate strategy and consulting group’s work? Where does it fit into Newmark’s broader deal-making? The idea is to become a strategic hub for the organization. stories.title: Prologis’ European Rival Segro Accepts $18.8B Takeover Offer
stories.excerpt: Prologis, the world’s largest industrial landlord, is about to get even bigger. The San Francisco-based real estate investment trust (REIT) has succeeded in its fourth offer to acquire rival Segro, the United Kingdom’s largest REIT, in a deal valuing Segro’s equity at roughly $18.8 billion. Prologis announced Tuesday that Segro’s once-resistant board would be recommending the deal. The combined portfolios’ global platform will total approximately $269 billion of assets under management. For the U.K., the deal means losing its largest REIT, the history of which stretches back more than a century. Segro’s portfolio spans approximately 117 million square feet across the U.K. and Europe, and has been made increasingly valuable by its expanding data center pipeline. “Prologis shares our conviction in the long-term structural drivers underpinning demand for modern logistics and data centre infrastructure,” David Sleath, CEO of Segro, said in a statement. “We believe the combination would bring together two highly complementary businesses and create a compelling platform, combining Segro’s exceptional portfolio and development pipeline with Prologis’ existing European business and global scale, customer franchise and operational capabilities, while retaining a shared commitment to disciplined capital allocation, customers and people,” Sleath added. Prologis’ European footprint is projected to grow by 47 percent with a 368 million-square-foot regional operating portfolio. The deal anticipates a combined European development pipeline of 13 million square feet and a 126 percent increase in Prologis’ European land bank. The acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to legal, regulatory and Segro shareholder approvals. bullets: Prologis acquires UK rival Segro for ~$18.8B equity value; combined AUM ~$269B globally
Segro portfolio: 117M sq ft UK/Europe; growing data center pipeline added strategic value
Consolidation creates world's largest industrial REIT with critical mass in logistics and data center
stories.summary: Prologis, the world's largest industrial REIT, has successfully completed its acquisition of Segro, the United Kingdom's largest REIT, at roughly $18.8 billion equity value. The combined platform will manage approximately $269 billion in global assets. Segro's 117 million square feet across the UK and Europe, bolstered by an expanding data center pipeline, drove strategic appeal. The deal marks the largest industrial consolidation in recent years and positions Prologis to dominate logistics and data center markets globally.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development; this is a pure-play industrial and data center transaction. However, large REIT consolidations can indirectly affect capital availability and cost of capital across real estate broadly. If consolidation reduces competition for development capital or increases institutional REIT focus on industrial at the expense of other sectors, multifamily developers may face relative tightness in high-yield debt markets. Monitor for capital flow shifts post-close, but near-term impact is limited.
